business_problem: E.ON needed a scalable and flexible replacement for a legacy contact center so it could support growing green-energy demand without disrupting customer service.
solution_summary: E.ON worked with IBM Consulting to replace a legacy contact-center stack with an omnichannel platform built on Amazon Connect in the AWS Cloud. IBM began with IBM Garage workshops, then used BizDevOps squads working in two- to three-week sprints to configure the platform across five specialist business units without disrupting service. The implementation connected voice, email, mobile and web channels for more than 1,000 agents and layered in AI-powered capabilities such as voice analysis, speech-to-text conversion and sentiment scoring. IBM Consulting also trained agents through hands-on practice before go-live and migrated units sequentially onto the platform. The architecture is less about a single AI model than about a scalable contact-center operating platform that uses cloud-native services and AI analysis to route, handle and assess large volumes of customer interactions.
products_used: IBM Consulting Services for AWS Cloud

solution_components.name: Amazon Connect
solution_components.role: Serves as the omnichannel contact-center platform used by agents across E.ON's business units.

solution_components.name: AWS Cloud
solution_components.role: Hosts the cloud infrastructure underpinning the new contact-center environment.

solution_components.name: IBM Consulting Services for AWS Cloud
solution_components.role: Configured and delivered the new contact-center platform across the different business units.

solution_components.name: IBM Garage
solution_components.role: Provided the workshop and agile delivery framework used to align stakeholders and iterate functionality.

data_flow: Customer voice, email, mobile and web interactions enter Amazon Connect on AWS, AI voice analysis and speech-to-text help route them to the right agent, and managers review sentiment-scored call data while agents handle the resulting omnichannel workload.
business_outcome: The project replaced the contact-center platform in under a year, now supports 120,000 monthly calls plus hundreds of thousands of emails and 70,000 live chats, and reduced costs through pay-as-you-grow SaaS licensing while improving wait times and first-time resolution.
architecture_clues: The rollout migrated five business units sequentially to minimize service disruption.
AI-powered voice analysis and sentiment scoring were layered into the contact-center workflow.
The platform uses pay-as-you-grow SaaS licensing rather than the legacy commercial model.
